root_idea.summary: The root centers on turning aside or deviating from a straight course.
root_idea.development: The same orientation extends to repeated or induced withdrawal and, in nominal usage, to curved or projecting irregularities such as prominences of mountains and horns.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I perfect citation form حَادَ rather than the Quranic imperfect تَحِيدُ.

senses.definition: To turn aside from something and recoil from, avoid, or shun it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb is construed with مِنْ and describes turning away from something with aversion or fear, rather than merely changing direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove or take away a person or thing, taking it far away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive removal construction used with بِـ, as in حَادَ بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut a thong or strip of leather lengthwise and make parts of it project beyond the rest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; the object is a thong or strip of skin or leather.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or move aside from, withdraw from, or avoid someone or something; also, to incline upon or against it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III; the sense of inclining upon or against is reported as an alternative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A projecting, prominent, or markedly curved part of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a mountain ledge or prominence, a knot or prominence in a horn, a projecting strap or thong, and prominent or curved body parts, including the hips, haunches, or thighs of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rugged part of a road.
An evil look accompanied by turning aside.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for looking at someone with aversion or hostility while turning away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner of walking marked by pride and self-conceit.
An epithet for an ass or she-ass that shies or turns aside readily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to an ass that shies at its shadow or frequently turns aside from things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pebbles thrown aside by the legs of a moving beast.
A call or command to turn aside or turn away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An indeclinable expression occurring in حِيدِي حَيَادِ, used when fighting begins or by one fleeing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One that turns away or departs much or repeatedly; an intensive epithet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reportedly applied to worldly prosperity that repeatedly declines or goes away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place to which one turns aside, withdraws, or goes away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An analogical noun of place, distinct from the same form's verbal-noun use.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Turning aside, departing, and avoiding are covered by the Quranic Form I sense.
The بِـ removal construction is separately represented.
Form II leather-cutting use is represented.
Form III withdrawal, avoidance, and alternative inclination use are represented.
Pointer-only reference to the Form I entry.
Physical prominence and projection uses are represented.
The specialized road use is represented.
The idiomatic evil-look use is represented.
The proud gait use is represented.
The term for pebbles cast aside by an animal is represented.
Pointer-only variant entry referring to حَيَدَى.
The conventional command to turn aside is represented.
The intensive epithet for frequent departure is represented.
Identifies the verbal-noun function only and adds no separate lexical branch.

cautions: The Quranic form is the imperfect active تَحِيدُ; the public headword حَادَ is the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
The spelling حَيِّدٌ is reported as a possible correction or variant of حَيَدَى, so it is retained only through the cross-reference and is not assigned an independent meaning.
